title: Komga
descript: Komga is a media server for comics, manga, bandes dessinees, magazines and eBooks. It scans your library folders, reads ComicInfo.xml (ComicRack) and EPUB metadata, and serves a web reader with collections, read lists, search, OPDS, Kobo Sync, KOReader sync and a REST API. The official Docker Hub image runs unmodified as a non-root container (uid 1000), and your books and database stay in the application data folder.
release_note: 1.30.2-1 - remediation of the 1.30.0-6 review. C4: complete privacy policy (retention, user rights, security measures, third-party sharing, deletion channel). C8: disclosed third-party endpoints (GitHub release check, Rakuten Kobo when Kobo Sync is enabled, Docker Hub pull, optional OIDC login). C9: description now matches the delivered app - there is no default account, you create the admin user on first start. T1: upstream 1.30.2. F7/S11/V1: gzip compression for the web UI, longer health-check start-up window, container pinned non-root with all capabilities dropped.
important: There is no default account: on first start open the app (http://NAS-IP:8024) and create your own admin user. Put comics/books in DockerAppData/komgadocker/data, then add that folder as a library in the web UI. Database, settings, thumbnails and logs live in .../config. Needs DockerEngine. Plain HTTP on the LAN - use a TLS reverse proxy before exposing it to the internet.

data_notes: `config` holds the database (database.sqlite), settings, generated thumbnails, fonts, the Lucene search index and logs. `data` is the library root that contains your comics/books. Copying both folders is a complete backup. Uninstalling the app keeps both folders unless you tick "delete data".
design_notes: **Non-root.** The upstream image declares no `USER`, so the package pins `user: "1000:1000"`, drops every capability (`cap_drop: [ALL]`) and sets `no-new-privileges`. Verified on hardware: the container reports uid 1000 and writes only below its own data folder.
**Two volumes, one port.** `/config` for state, `/data` for the library; only port 25600 is published (host 8024).

**Compressed web UI.** Spring Boot gzip compression is enabled through `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS`, which cuts the reader's initial JavaScript from about 3.5 MB to about 0.85 MB and keeps the first paint fast on slow links.
**Health check** probes `/` on 25600 with a 180 s start-up window, because a cold JVM start on a NAS takes 40-60 s.
**Fixed image tag**, Docker Hub only, no privileged mode, no host network, no Docker socket.
limitations: Komga does not create a comic library. Put your files into `DockerAppData/komgadocker/data` and add the library folder in the web UI.
There is no default account: the first visit asks you to create the admin user (the server stays unclaimed until then).

Komga 1.30 reads metadata from the files themselves (ComicInfo.xml, EPUB) and from manual edits. It has no built-in online metadata scraper, so nothing in the default flow contacts a metadata provider.
The database is SQLite by default. Very large libraries may benefit from more memory; set `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS` if you need a larger heap.
Plain HTTP on the LAN; do not expose the published port to the internet without a TLS reverse proxy.
